repo_prior_art.cite: No catalogue entry gives a fixed-design Gaussian, outcome-independent nested-support SOCP for simultaneous honest widths.

published_prior_art.cite: CattaneoFengPalombaTitiunik2025 gives non-asymptotic staggered prediction intervals and conic implementations, but not this prescribed Bonferroni width objective.

repo_prior_art.cite: panel_bhar_proxy_modulus_frontier concerns a nonparametric generated-proxy minimax problem, not finite Gaussian synthetic-control rectangles.

published_prior_art.cite: ArmstrongKolesar2018 is scalar convex-class Gaussian CI theory; BenMichaelFellerRothstein2022 uses fixed donor pools; CattaneoFengPalombaTitiunik2025 does not give the optimized nested-support width sandwich.
BenMichaelFellerRothstein2022 defines the same shrinking donor sets, while the asserted value inequality is the immediate feasible-set consequence.
Pataki2013 and JeyakumarKumLee2008 supply the generic facial-reduction and conic weak-duality machinery; the statement is its direct application.

repo_prior_art.cite: No catalogue proposal studies strict nested-versus-deep SOCP values with facial-reduced certificates.

published_prior_art.cite: Pataki2013 and JeyakumarKumLee2008 do not state an iff certificate for these two support-restricted synthetic-control programs.
This is a transparent equality-of-feasible-sets boundary case implicit in BenMichaelFellerRothstein2022.
ArmstrongKolesar2018 provides the scalar known-variance Gaussian convex-class benchmark; this proposition is correctly framed as compatibility rather than novelty.

novelty_flags.label: Comparator promise for BenMichaelFellerRothstein2022 / Open-ended Question 1
novelty_flags.one_line: The OEQ compares two newly defined Gamma programs, not Ben-Michael–Feller–Rothstein's published partially pooled estimator, so it does not deliver the promised iff comparison against that comparator.

soundness_flags.label: oeq:degenerate-iff-certificate
soundness_flags.one_line: A finite outward-rounded certificate is not defined for unrestricted real-valued x, L, delta, and SigmaQ: specify an input representation, a conic encoding, and certificate-verification arithmetic.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:socp-coverage and thm:constant-factor-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: All coverage and frontier claims are conditional on the known-covariance fixed-design Gaussian experiment and outcome-independent deterministic weights.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The proposal claims finite-sample honesty and the width comparison only within this declared Gaussian deterministic-linear decision class.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:constant-factor-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The comparison concerns the exact robust rectangle W_s and the Bonferroni surrogate Gamma_s; the strict-gap OEQ concerns Gamma only.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Any strict-support conclusion is an SOCP-frontier conclusion unless a separate result transfers it to W_nested < W_deep.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 2.2, pp. 355–356, especially the donor-pool discussion following the definition of D_jk
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines D_jk={i:T_i>T_j+k}, says the composition varies with event time, and explicitly focuses on fixed D_jK although its estimator need not impose that restriction.

source_verification_receipts.version: Review of Economics and Statistics article PDF, DOI 10.1162/rest_a_01588
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 4–5 and 23–24; Remark 2 and equation (4.6) discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article gives non-asymptotic staggered synthetic-control uncertainty quantification, valid joint inference across periods, and conic implementations of its error-bound programs.
The paper derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds for a scalar linear functional over a convex regression class under normal errors with known variance.

source_verification_receipts.version: Publisher-formatted author copy of Probability Theory and Related Fields 162, 2015
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorems 2–3 compare maxima and give anti-concentration under arbitrary covariance structures with positive coordinate variances; they do not themselves posit a Loewner covariance band.
The paper develops facial reduction and extended strong duals for conic linear programs without ordinary constraint qualifications.
The article gives closed-cone conditions for Farkas lemmas and necessary-and-sufficient strong-duality characterizations for second-order cone programs.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Either state a theorem directly comparing the proposed nested rule with the published Ben-Michael–Feller–Rothstein partially pooled estimator, or change all BMF language from an extension/frontier comparator to an informed-by support-geometry anchor.

Restrict the strict-certificate OEQ to rational or algebraic input data and define a verifier for primal feasibility, facial-reduced dual feasibility, and directed-rounding intervals; then state its bit-complexity or termination guarantee.
Add a worked staggered-adoption instance with a certified positive Gamma_deep−Gamma_nested gap and report why its fixed-pool comparator is substantively relevant.

recommended_next_step: Revise the comparator claim and make the certificate computational model precise, then return the repaired field-tier kernel to Stage 0.
